name: CDP and Runtime.enable detection signals — the family of page-side checks that reveal an attached Chrome DevTools Protocol client. Sub-signals commonly named separately: the Runtime.enable / ExecutionContextId leak (Vastel, June 2024), the console.debug error-getter serialisation side channel (the 'classic' CDP signal), CDP-attach timing side channels, and the older navigator.webdriver flag which is adjacent but distinct. Sometimes called 'CDP fingerprinting' or 'the Runtime.Enable leak'.
kind: A detection technique family, i.e. an adversarial capability, not a library or standard. The individual signals are implemented inside commercial anti-bot JavaScript bundles (Cloudflare Turnstile, DataDome, Kasada, PerimeterX/HUMAN, Castle) and reimplemented in open probes (CreepJS, Scrapfly's automation detector, deviceandbrowserinfo.com). Its counterparts on the defensive side are patches (rebrowser-patches, nodriver, SeleniumBase CDP Mode) rather than standards.
maturity: Production and actively evolving, with one sub-signal now dead. The ExecutionContextId variant is confirmed in production: identical sessions with Runtime.enable active receive an immediate Cloudflare Turnstile / DataDome challenge, and the challenge disappears when Runtime.enable is not sent. The console.debug error-getter variant was neutralised at the engine level by two V8 commits in May 2025 ('Avoid error side effects in DevTools', 7 May 2025; 'Apply getter guard throughout error preview', 9 May 2025) which added a getErrorProperty() guard preventing user-defined getters from firing during DevTools preview — the flag now never flips, and Castle's public write-up notes the signal degraded silently, with detectors continuing to ship a check that had stopped working. That silent degradation is itself the most instructive fact in this item.
license: Not applicable to the detection signals themselves. The evasion side is: rebrowser-patches (patches to Puppeteer/Playwright) and nodriver are permissively licensed open source; Camoufox is a patched-Firefox distribution [uncertain — exact license]. None is adoptable here because this project does not drive Chrome.
keeps_and_discards: Not an extraction approach — it extracts nothing from the page and preserves no content. What it 'keeps' is a boolean plus, in richer implementations, a confidence score and a timing distribution. The relevance to a content pipeline is entirely upstream: if the signal fires, the page may serve a challenge, a stub, or deliberately altered content instead of the real document, so the signal determines WHETHER there is anything to extract at all. This is the class of failure that produces a syntactically valid, structurally clean, entirely worthless fold — a Turnstile interstitial folds beautifully.
structure_preserved: None; the signal has no document representation. The second-order effect on structure is the one that matters: a challenged page substitutes a small, shallow, script-driven interstitial for the real document, so the fold's structural output collapses from hundreds of nodes to a handful. That collapse is detectable without any structure classifier — a sudden order-of-magnitude drop in trie node count for a URL that previously folded richly is a structure-agnostic alarm, and it is arguably the cheapest gate-state detector available to this project.
interactive_elements: The signal treats controls only as challenge surfaces. Where it bears on this project: a challenged page presents controls (a checkbox, a slider, an 'I am human' widget) that are indistinguishable at the tag-plus-interactivity level from legitimate page controls. A structure-agnostic sensor cannot tell a Turnstile checkbox from a consent checkbox from a newsletter opt-in — all three are an interactive element with a label — and refusing to name regions means refusing to name this one too. The honest resolution is not a classifier but a request-level fact: a Turnstile or DataDome challenge is accompanied by a characteristic third-party request (challenges.cloudflare.com, js.datadome.co / captcha-delivery.com), and that is an address-keyed peripheral observation, not a structure heuristic.
interactive_state_fidelity: Not applicable to the signal itself. The relevant consequence for state fidelity is severe and often missed: when an anti-bot bundle decides a session is automated, it may not block outright but may instead degrade — lazily-loaded content never loads, infinite scroll never advances, personalisation never applies. The DOM then reports aria-busy states, aria-expanded=false, and skeleton placeholders that are all technically accurate and semantically wrong, because the page is in a permanently pre-hydration state. 'Tag plus interactivity' faithfully records a page that never finished becoming itself, at full token cost and zero information value. The only defence is the same divergence check that applies to targeted serving: fold the same URL from two identities and compare.
layout_awareness: The detection signals read no page geometry. Adjacent signals in the same bundles do — window.outerHeight minus window.innerHeight equal to zero is a long-standing headless indicator, and screen/viewport mismatch is checked — but the CDP-specific signals are protocol-level and geometry-free. Notably, this means the project's no-layout-in-the-fold constraint neither helps nor hurts here; the exposure is entirely in the actuator's connection to the browser, which is exactly where the constraint says such things belong.
javascript_required: Absolutely required on the detection side — every one of these signals is JavaScript running in the page. That is the structural fact this project must sit with: a no-mocks sensor reads real pages in a real browser with real script execution, so every anti-bot bundle on the page runs and evaluates the session. There is no read-only mode. The corollary is that the project's exposure to this signal family is not a function of how it folds the DOM but purely of how the browser is driven, which makes it an actuator-layer concern in the project's own vocabulary.
evaluation_method: Establishment of these signals is unusually good for the security-blog genre because it is differential and behavioural rather than asserted. The canonical experiment — run by Rebrowser and reproduced widely — holds everything constant except whether Runtime.enable is sent, and observes whether Cloudflare Turnstile / DataDome issues a challenge. That is a clean A/B against a live production detector, which is a stronger form of evidence than a vendor blog post, because the oracle is the vendor's own deployed system rather than the researcher's claim. Castle's May-2025 finding was established the same way: probe the signal against current Chrome, observe the flag no longer flips, then trace to the V8 commits. Detection-side implementations are further verified against open probe pages (CreepJS, Scrapfly automation detector) that report per-signal results.
corpus_size_and_origins: There is no corpus in the extraction sense and this is a genuine evidentiary weakness. The differential experiments are single-site or few-site: 'a Cloudflare-protected page', 'a DataDome-protected page'. No published measurement states what fraction of the top-1M web deploys CDP-specific detection, how it varies by archetype, or how detection thresholds differ by geography. Adjacent measurement gives an order of magnitude — anti-bot vendors collectively front a large minority of commercial sites, with Cloudflare alone in front of a double-digit percentage of the top million — but that is coverage of the vendor, not of this specific signal within the vendor's bundle. Anything quoted about prevalence of CDP detection specifically is inference, not measurement. [uncertain]
reported_precision_recall: No precision/recall figures are published by anyone, and the reason is adversarial: publishing the operating point of a bot detector tells the adversary where to sit. What is stated qualitatively and is credible: the Runtime.enable signal has near-zero false positives against ordinary browsing, with the single documented false-positive class being users with DevTools genuinely open — estimated at under 0.1% of sessions, and itself a suspicious-enough bucket that vendors are content to challenge it. The recall side is now poor for the console.debug variant (effectively zero on Chrome post-May-2025) and remains high for the ExecutionContextId variant against unpatched Puppeteer/Playwright/Selenium, and near zero against nodriver and SeleniumBase CDP Mode, which avoid Runtime.enable entirely.
independent_oracle: Yes, and it is the strongest feature of the evidence base. The production anti-bot system is an oracle that shares no assumptions with the researcher: it either challenges the session or it does not, and it was built by a party with a commercial interest in being right. Toggling one protocol command and watching a third party's challenge appear and vanish is about as independent as web-security evidence gets. The oracle is opaque (you learn that something was detected, not which signal fired) and non-stationary (vendors update weekly), but it is not circular.
evidence_independence: Mixed and worth reading carefully. The best evidence comes from parties selling the opposite of what they demonstrate: Vastel's original disclosure came while he was at DataDome (a detection vendor publishing a detection technique — self-interested toward exaggeration), while Rebrowser and Scrapfly are evasion vendors publishing the same technique (self-interested toward exaggerating the problem their product solves). That the two opposed commercial camps agree on the mechanism is a meaningful cross-check. Castle's finding that the classic signal silently died is the most credible single item, because it is a detection vendor publishing that a detection signal stopped working — against its own commercial interest. Nothing here is peer-reviewed; this literature lives entirely in vendor blogs, and it moves faster than academic publication can track.
page_archetype_coverage: Not measured per archetype, but the deployment skew is strong and predictable from what anti-bot products are sold to protect: e-commerce, ticketing, travel, financial services, streaming and job boards carry heavy anti-bot instrumentation; documentation sites, government pages, academic archives and personal sites carry essentially none. For this project's corpus this is the dominant consideration and it cuts favourably — an archive/documentation-leaning corpus will encounter CDP detection rarely, and a commercial-page corpus will encounter it constantly. Any aggregate success rate over a mixed corpus is therefore meaningless without an archetype breakdown, and the project should report fold success rate separately for anti-bot-fronted and unprotected origins.
script_and_locale_behaviour: Script and locale are irrelevant to the signal, which operates on protocol state rather than text. One second-order locale effect is documented anecdotally rather than measured: anti-bot systems weight geographic and ASN reputation heavily, so an identical automated session is challenged at very different rates from a residential European IP versus a datacenter IP, independent of any CDP signal. That confound must be controlled in any local measurement of detection rate, or the project will attribute to its driving method what is actually attributable to its egress address. [uncertain — no quantified figures located]
leaks_outward: The signal discloses one high-value bit to the page — 'this session is instrumented' — and in richer bundles a confidence score, a timing profile, and the fact that a specific evasion patch is or is not present. Second-order, it discloses to the page's third-party anti-bot vendor, who aggregates across their entire customer base, so a single detected session on one site can inform reputation at every other site the vendor fronts. That cross-site aggregation is the underappreciated leak: the disclosure is not to one origin but to a network. For a sensor reading a corpus of 92+ hosts per run, a detection on one host can plausibly degrade service on others sharing a vendor.
mechanism_detectability: This is the item where the project's first tension is decided, and the evidence is specific enough to settle it. FIRST, the direct answer: this project does not drive Chrome, so the CDP signal family does not apply to it at all. Firefox's CDP implementation is deprecated in favour of WebDriver BiDi, and Marionette is not CDP — no Runtime.enable is ever sent, no ExecutionContextId leak exists, and the V8 error-getter path is a V8 concern with no SpiderMonkey analogue. The entire ExecutionContextId attack surface is absent by construction. SECOND, what DOES apply: navigator.webdriver. Firefox sets it true whenever a WebDriver session is active — since Bugzilla 1696425 it is bound to the WebDriver (Marionette/BiDi) session lifetime rather than to the marionette.enabled preference, meaning it is on for the duration of the session by specification. It is a single standardised boolean property read, defined by W3C WebDriver, documented on MDN, and it is the first check in essentially every commercial anti-bot bundle; Google is documented as blocking on navigator.webdriver === true alone. It is not a timing channel, not a heuristic, not probabilistic: it is a flag the browser volunteers. THIRD, the comparison the tension asks for. attachShadow patching is detectable by Function.prototype.toString on Element.prototype.attachShadow (a patched function does not stringify as native code), by descriptor comparison, and by timing. Native-function integrity checking IS deployed in production anti-tamper and anti-bot bundles — it is standard practice in obfuscated commercial bundles and appears in Kasada- and DataDome-class scripts — but the observed target set for those checks is the well-known evasion targets: navigator property descriptors, canvas getContext and toDataURL, fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebGL getParameter, Function.prototype.toString itself. Element.prototype.attachShadow is not on the commonly-observed list, because patching it is not a common evasion and there is no commercial motive to look for it. VERDICT: the detectability ordering is the inverse of the project's assumption. navigator.webdriver under Marionette is a specified, universally-read, zero-cost boolean that fires on 100% of sessions; attachShadow patching is a generically-possible integrity check that in current production is not aimed at attachShadow. Refusing attachShadow patching on detectability grounds while accepting Marionette is therefore INCONSISTENT AS ARGUED. The constraint should be re-grounded — encapsulation-honouring (a closed root is an author's explicit boundary), page-stability (the patch must win the race against every page script and breaks pages that probe their own roots), and maintenance (the patch is a permanent fight with engine internals) are all sound and sufficient reasons, and they do not depend on a detectability claim that the evidence contradicts. If detectability genuinely is the operative principle, Marionette must be addressed first — which in practice means either accepting differentiated service honestly, or moving to a patched build such as Camoufox that suppresses the flag at the C++ level, which is itself a far more invasive form of the same lying the project refuses elsewhere.
countermeasures: On the Chrome side, three tiers, listed for completeness rather than adoption: rebrowser-patches (replace Runtime.enable with Page.createIsolatedWorld or an enable/disable toggle, at the cost of isolated-world variable access or a residual detection window); nodriver and SeleniumBase CDP Mode (avoid the command entirely, connecting and disconnecting the driver around actions); Camoufox (C++-level fingerprint patching of Firefox). On the Firefox/Marionette side the countermeasure surface is much thinner and this is a genuine advantage: there is no Runtime.enable to hide. The remaining exposure is navigator.webdriver, and the honest options are only two — leave it true and accept that some origins will serve differently, or run a patched build that suppresses it. The project's own commitments point to the first: identify honestly, record gate state, and treat differentiated service as data rather than as an obstacle. That position also aligns with the Web Bot Auth direction, where declaring agency is the intended posture rather than a failure.
measured_fidelity_cost: No hardening arm here has a fidelity cost, because none of these are hardening — they are detection, and the project's response to them is a policy choice rather than a filter. What this item does supply is a missing measurement the project should run and currently has not: a per-origin fold-success and fold-size comparison between an anti-bot-fronted subset and an unprotected subset of the corpus, against the existing 0.07% null-control floor. The prediction is that anti-bot-fronted origins will show fold-size drops far outside the 2.3x-of-floor band that every hardening arm stayed inside on saved pages — not tens of percent but orders of magnitude, because a challenged page is a different document. If that prediction holds, detection is not a hardening-cost phenomenon at all and belongs in a separate ledger from block_trackers' 10.49%. The saved-corpus 0.16% figure is silent on this by construction, since saved pages carry no live anti-bot evaluation.
gate_state_at_capture: This item makes gate-state recording non-optional. A CAPTCHA or interstitial IS a gate state, it is the one gate state most likely to be produced BY the act of automated capture rather than found in the wild, and it is invisible in the fold as anything other than a small clean document. Recording it requires no structure classifier: the presence of a request to a known challenge endpoint (challenges.cloudflare.com, js.datadome.co, captcha-delivery.com, an hCaptcha or Turnstile origin), an HTTP 403 with a vendor header, or an order-of-magnitude fold-size collapse relative to a prior capture of the same URL are all address-keyed or size-keyed observations that sit cleanly in the peripheral. The project should treat 'challenged' as a first-class gate state alongside consent, paywall and login.
determinism: The signals are deterministic in mechanism — the same protocol state produces the same observable — but the VERDICT is not, because production detectors combine the signal with reputation, behaviour and rate. The same automated session can be challenged on one request and pass on the next. This is the important reliability property: an experiment that toggles Runtime.enable and observes a challenge is reproducible in aggregate but not per-request, and any single-run result is noise. The project must treat every detection measurement as requiring repetition, which is expensive, and must not read a single successful capture as evidence of non-detection.
determinism_across_versions: Poor, and demonstrated to be poor by the single most useful fact in this item: a widely-deployed signal was silently killed by two V8 commits in May 2025, and detectors continued shipping it without noticing. Engine-version drift here does not degrade a signal gradually, it terminates it discontinuously, and the failure is invisible from the detector's side because a signal that never fires looks identical to a signal facing no adversaries. Any capability in this space has a shelf life measured in browser release cycles. For this project the transferable lesson is about its own probes rather than about CDP: any check the project builds that depends on engine-internal behaviour needs a positive control that proves the check can still fire, or it will silently become a no-op exactly as this one did.
reproducibility: The differential experiment is reproducible in method — anyone can toggle the command and watch for a challenge — but not in result across time, because the vendor side changes continuously and unannounced. Nothing here is archivable: there is no fixed corpus, the detectors are remote and mutable, and a result from 2024 does not hold in 2026 (the console.debug variant is the proof). Findings in this area should be dated on sight and re-verified before being relied on, and this item's own contents should be re-checked rather than cited in a year.
failure_modes: For the detector: false positives on genuine DevTools users; complete failure against drivers that never send Runtime.enable; and the silent-death mode already described. For an automated reader on the receiving end, the failure modes are more varied and worse than outright blocking. Outright block (403, challenge page) is the benign case because it is loud. The malign cases are: soft-degradation, where content loads partially and the fold looks plausible; shadow-banning, where the page serves a stale or reduced dataset with normal structure; rate-throttling that manifests as timeouts attributed to the network; and delayed challenge, where the first N captures succeed and capture N+1 begins failing, silently splitting a corpus into pre- and post-detection halves with no marker at the boundary.
failure_visibility: Silent by design on both sides, and this is the property that should most concern this project. Anti-bot vendors deliberately prefer invisible evaluation and soft degradation over visible challenges, because visible challenges teach the adversary. DataDome and PerimeterX explicitly inject scripts that evaluate sessions with no visible challenge at all. The consequence is that a corpus can be quietly poisoned with degraded captures that carry every marker of success: HTTP 200, well-formed HTML, a clean fold, plausible token count. The project's standing refusal of silent degradation applies here with full force and demands an explicit positive control — a known-good content assertion per origin, or a cross-identity diff — because absence of an error is not evidence of a good capture.
scale_limits: Detection cost is negligible per session for the detector. The scaling asymmetry runs against the reader: detection confidence is superlinear in request volume from one identity, because reputation systems aggregate. One capture of one page is nearly always fine; 3,082 requests per run to 92+ hosts is a volume at which reputation effects dominate any per-request signal, and the identity — IP, ASN, TLS fingerprint, cookie state — becomes the deciding factor rather than anything in the browser. The practical limit is therefore not a per-page cost curve but a per-identity budget, and it is crossed at a scale this project's corpus already operates at.
delta_cost_model: Not applicable in the extraction sense; there is no incremental structure to maintain. There is one useful adjacent observation for the project's own delta model: an anti-bot challenge is precisely the change class that a delta model must be able to detect as out-of-model. If a URL that previously folded to thousands of nodes now folds to forty, an incremental update would report a very large delta — which is correct, and which means the delta magnitude itself is a usable challenge detector requiring no classifier. Making that explicit is worthwhile: define a delta-magnitude threshold above which a capture is flagged for gate-state review rather than merged, and the O(delta) machinery pays for a safety property it was not designed for.
reanchoring_stability: Not applicable directly — no node identity is at stake. Indirectly, challenge interstitials are the worst adversary of re-anchoring stability that exists: they replace the entire document, so every anchor in the trie for that URL fails at once. That total-failure pattern is diagnostically distinct from ordinary DOM churn, where anchors fail individually and partially. A re-anchoring layer should therefore distinguish 'most anchors for this URL failed simultaneously' (document substitution — a gate event, do not re-anchor, flag the capture) from 'some anchors failed' (ordinary drift — re-anchor normally). That distinction is cheap, needs no page-structure knowledge, and turns a re-anchoring metric into a gate detector.
adversarial_exposure: The signal itself preserves no content and so conceals nothing. Its contribution to this project's second tension is to enlarge the threat model in a direction the concealment taxonomy usually omits: content that was never served. Rendering-based concealment (display:none, 0px, off-screen) hides content that IS in the DOM; anti-bot differentiation prevents content from entering the DOM, or substitutes different content, based on who is reading. No filter — Unicode-level, DOM-level, semantic, or geometric — detects that, because the evidence is not in the document. The only detector is comparative: the same URL, two identities, two folds, one diff. This is a layout-free, structure-agnostic check the project can implement with machinery it already has, and it defends against a class that geometry-based concealment filtering also cannot touch. It is a genuine argument that the layout-blind fold's ceiling is not as low as it looks, because part of the concealment problem is not addressable by ANY single-capture method.
provenance_carrying: The signal carries no content provenance. What it argues for is one additional provenance field on the project's own captures: the session identity under which the capture was taken — profile id, egress address class, driver mode, and whether navigator.webdriver was true. Without it, a corpus mixes captures taken under different detection outcomes with no way to separate them after the fact, and any cross-capture diff becomes uninterpretable. This is a small, cheap addition to a key that already carries url : xpath : markdown : content, and it belongs in the peripheral rather than the fold.
roundtrip_safety: Not applicable — nothing is serialised. One narrow note: challenge pages frequently contain heavily obfuscated inline script and long base64 payloads, and a fold that captures them will carry very high-entropy text with no linguistic content. If a serialise-parse-serialise fixed-point test is used as an oracle-free fidelity metric, challenge pages will pass it trivially while carrying zero information, which is a reminder that roundtrip stability is a necessary and emphatically not sufficient fidelity condition.
token_budget_and_ordering: A challenge page is small — typically well under a thousand tokens — so it never stresses the budget, and that is exactly the hazard: it fits comfortably, reads as a complete document, and gives an SLM no cue that it is looking at a wall rather than a page. If an interstitial is folded and passed forward, the model will confidently reason about the wrong document. Any gate state, and 'challenged' most of all, must be surfaced as an explicit marker in whatever the model sees, near the front of the context where it will be read, rather than being inferable only from the content's oddity.
representation_cost: Near zero for the artifacts of detection. The real cost is a discarded capture and a wasted request budget, plus, in the soft-degradation case, a full-price capture of a partially-hydrated page that costs full tokens for a fraction of the content — the worst tokens-per-unit-information ratio in the whole pipeline.
what_could_be_adopted: Nothing from the Chrome-side evasion toolchain, which is inapplicable. Four things are worth taking. (1) The differential-experiment method itself: hold everything constant, toggle exactly one driver-level property, and use a production detector as the oracle — this is the correct experimental design for any claim the project makes about its own detectability, and it is cheap. (2) The positive-control discipline that the May-2025 silent death makes vivid: every environment-dependent check needs a control proving it can still fire. (3) Challenge-state detection via address-keyed request observation plus fold-size collapse, which yields a first-class 'challenged' gate state without any structure classifier. (4) The cross-identity fold diff as the only available detector for served-content differentiation, reusing the trie comparison the project already needs.
constraint_violation_ledger: structure_agnosticism: ADOPTABLE AS-IS — the derived gate detectors (request-endpoint observation, fold-size collapse, delta magnitude, simultaneous anchor failure) are all size- or address-keyed and name no region; nothing here requires a classifier. no_layout_in_the_fold: ADOPTABLE AS-IS — every signal is protocol- or request-level, and the geometry-based headless indicators in adjacent bundles concern the actuator's window configuration, which is properly peripheral. o_delta: ADOPTABLE AS-IS and mildly additive — delta magnitude becomes a gate signal at no extra cost. no_mocks: ADOPTABLE AS-IS, with a cost this item makes explicit — real browsers on real pages are evaluated by real anti-bot systems, so a fraction of any live corpus is silently degraded, and the no-mocks stance therefore obliges the project to add positive controls it does not currently have. closed_shadow_roots_stay_closed: NEGATIVE ORACLE ONLY, and the strongest such finding in this research set — the constraint's detectability justification is refuted by the evidence here (navigator.webdriver under Marionette is a specified, universally-read boolean firing on every session; attachShadow-targeted integrity checks are not in the observed production target set), so the constraint must be re-justified on encapsulation, stability and maintenance grounds or applied consistently to Marionette. The constraint's CONCLUSION survives; its stated REASON does not. Overall verdict for the item: negative oracle only as a body of technique, adoptable as-is as a set of measurement disciplines.
governance_signal_handling: Entirely orthogonal in mechanism and directly opposed in spirit. CDP detection is unilateral, undeclared and adversarial on both sides — the site does not announce that it is testing, and the client does not announce that it is automated. The governance stack (robots.txt, Content Signals, ai.txt, AIPREF, Web Bot Auth, HTTP 402) proposes replacing that arms race with declaration: the site states its terms in a machine-readable way, and the agent identifies itself cryptographically. Web Bot Auth is the direct substitute for this entire signal family — a signed request makes detection unnecessary — and adopting it would make the project's navigator.webdriver exposure moot, since it would be declaring automation anyway. That is the coherent long-run position and it resolves the first tension in the same stroke: if the project identifies as an agent, the detectability of Marionette stops being a cost and the attachShadow refusal rests entirely on encapsulation grounds, where it belongs.
legal_basis_and_pii_posture: Two distinct exposures. Outbound: an anti-bot vendor evaluating the session collects device and behavioural data about the operator's machine across every customer site, which is processing of the operator's personal data by a third party, with the operator as data subject rather than controller — no obligation created, but a real exposure worth acknowledging. Inbound and more consequential: deliberately evading a technical access-control measure is legally distinct from merely scraping, and touches computer-misuse statutes (CFAA in the US, the Computer Misuse Act in the UK, Article 6 of the EU Cybercrime-implementing law) in a way that reading an open page does not — hiQ v. LinkedIn narrowed the CFAA exposure for public data but did not bless circumvention of technical barriers, and EU member-state law is less settled. Under EDPB Guidelines 03/2026 the regulated act is the persistent storage of scraped content, so a capture obtained by circumventing a challenge is doubly exposed: the storage needs a lawful basis and the acquisition method is an aggravating factor in the balancing test for legitimate interest. The posture that follows is the conservative and coherent one: do not circumvent, record 'challenged' as a terminal gate state, and let the corpus carry an honest hole rather than a laundered capture.
